transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (Head of ML, Cascade), Anika Bose (CTO), Derek Wu (Infra Eng), Meena Shah (Product)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align success criteria, workload sizing, and deployment decision heatmap (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer wants clear acceptance criteria for latency, throughput and cost targets plus security gating for Private VPC. Agreed to run an initial hosted benchmark with sample workload, then re-evaluate Dedicated/Private if constraints demand.

Topics: acceptance criteria, benchmark plan, timeline, VPC/KMS, SLA tradeoffs, model variants, cost burn rate

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Morgan: alright, thanks everyone for joining, uh, i'll kick off — i'm Morgan from Redwood, AE for your account. today's goal is to map out the pilot rubric, right? what does success look like, what we'll benchmark, and the hosting pathways.
[00:18] Carlos: thanks Morgan, yeah appreciate it. quick context — we want to embed an assistant into our service manuals and shop-floor tablets. expected bursty QPS, mid-to-high concurrency during shift changes. security is top of mind, and residency for eu is later but not first phase.
[00:36] Priya: hi all, i'm Priya on the SE side. couple clarifying q's: what's target latency p95 you're aiming for and what model sizes roughly? and do you have a current baseline?
[00:48] Anika: baseline is our in-house small LLM at about p95 800ms for 4k context; we want <300ms p95 for end user interactive feel. accuracy-wise we need parity or better on our rubric prompts, and cost ideally under $X per 1M tokens — we can give a number offline.
[01:10] Morgan: got it, so candidate success metrics: p95 <= 300ms, throughput to support 250 concurrent sessions at peak (we'll translate to QPS), and quality pass-rate >= 95% on your prompt eval set. sound reasonable?
[01:27] Carlos: yes that maps. also need failover plan if region capacity is constrained, and audit logs (are we covered by SOC2?).
[01:35] Priya: Redwood's hosted is SOC2, yeah, we have a security pack — will send. for hosting tradeoffs quick summary: hosted = fastest time to value, easiest for benchmarking; dedicated = reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower p95 variance; private = VPC/air-gapped with K-M-S integrations and on-prem options but longer setup.
[02:10] Derek: can you unpack the dedicated capacity bit — we care about consistent tail latency, not just mean. how do you price reserved pools vs pay-as-you-go?
[02:25] Morgan: pricing depends on commit; we can run a 6-week pilot on hosted then transition to dedicated reserved pool if throughput or latency needs it. reserved gives a committed throughput SLA and lower per-token cost in many cases. we'll include an example pricing band in the SOW.
[02:44] Priya: for benchmarking we propose 2 phases: Phase A hosted functional + latency/throughput runs with your sample payload (48h anonymized) to get baseline numbers; Phase B if we hit gating limits then run a dedicated/private exercise that covers VPC peering, egress, and K-M-S key rotation.
[03:05] Anika: timeline question: how long to get meaningful numbers?
[03:09] Priya: Phase A can run in 3-5 business days once we have the sample data and a service account for the hosted runs. full analysis and bench report in 7 business days. Phase B (if needed) typically adds ~3 weeks for network setup and validation for dedicated or private.
[03:29] Meena: and acceptance criteria we should write down so procurement can sign off. Carlos: are we okay with the p95 and quality thresholds?
[03:38] Carlos: yes but add a reliability SLO — target 99.9% availability for inference endpoints during pilot window. also we want token cost estimates.
[03:49] Morgan: we'll include availability SLO goals and, importantly, the fallback plan: multi-model routing and automatic degrade to a smaller quantized model to preserve latency while reducing cost in high load.
[04:10] Derek: on the network side, if we go private we need VPC peering and private link — any known constraints? and KMS integration for customer-managed keys?
[04:21] Priya: we support customer K-M-S integration for private. note: transcription may show KMS as K-M-S — sorry — but yes, we can key manage, rotation, and H-S-M in certain on-prem builds. VPC peering windows typically require your infra team to set firewall rules; it's not trivial but it's routine.
[04:48] Anika: for our risk committee we need audit logs per request, RBAC controls, and retention options. how granular are your logs?
[04:58] Morgan: per-request tracing is available; console shows token-level cost and request traces. we'll redact PII for the bench runs if needed, and include longer-term log retention as an add-on.
[05:15] Priya: turning to workload sizing — Carlos, can you share expected QPS and average tokens per request? even rough numbers help us size GPU types (e.g., small batched gpus vs larger instance series).
[05:27] Carlos: typical request is 120 tokens, sometimes up to 1k for long troubleshooting threads. baseline QPS average 15, spiking to 200 for 60-90 seconds during shift switchover.
[05:39] Priya: perfect. for that profile we usually test both batching modes: low-latency continuous batching and throughput batched runs. We'll capture token/sec and tokens per GPU metrics and recommend whether quantized LLMs on shared hosted infra or a dedicated A100-style pool is better.
[06:00] Morgan: cost guidance — hosted pilot will show per-token cost; if cost too high we'll look at quantization and dedicated reservations.
[06:08] Derek: any chance of model output regressions with quantization? we cannot accept quality drops >5% on your evaluation set.
[06:16] Priya: agreed — quality regression guardrails in Redwood Optimize detect drift by comparing eval prompts across model variants. we can pin to a golden model and set alerts for regressions >3-5%.
[06:31] Anika: benchmarks — what exact metrics will you include in the bench report?
[06:35] Priya: the bench report will include p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (reqs/sec), tokens/sec per GPU, tail latency distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, and quality pass-rate on your eval prompt set. we'll also include a recommended deployment mode and configuration.
[06:58] Morgan: we'll also run a failure-mode test: sudden spike to 400 QPS for 2 minutes to see graceful degradation and fallback to smaller model variants.
[07:08] Carlos: that makes sense. procurement wants SLA language and breach remedies for the pilot; is there a lightweight pilot SLO we can sign?
[07:18] Morgan: yes, pilot SLOs are standard — we'll share a one-page SLO with availability targets, support response time, and escalation path.
[07:28] Meena: who will lead the bench execution?
[07:30] Priya: SE-run with customer validation. Priya and team will run hosted benches, Morgan will manage procurement and SOW, Carlos and Derek provide artifacts and network input.
[07:40] Anika: if hosted looks good but VPC is preferred for compliance later, how long to switch?
[07:47] Priya: moving from hosted to private with VPC peering usually takes 2-4 weeks for network approvals and key integrations. Dedicated reserved pools can be shorter if no VPC needed.
[07:59] Derek: note that we have strict egress limits to vendor infra — we need to see bandwidth and egress cost estimates.
[08:06] Morgan: we'll include egress estimates. also want to call out automatic caching strategies (prefix/K-V cache) to reduce token cost for repeated lookups — that can dramatically lower burn for your use case.
[08:25] Carlos: K-V cache? sorry transcription might show K V cash — but yes, explain how caching affects latency and cost.
[08:33] Priya: KV caching stores prefix KV states so repeated conversational tokens are not recomputed; in practice for troubleshooting flows with repeated context it can cut token consumption by 30-60% and improve tail latency. We'll capture caching impact in the bench.
[08:53] Anika: any red flags you see given our numbers?
[08:57] Priya: main risks: long tail requests at 1k tokens cause GPU memory pressure and increase p95; second, network peering delays when moving to private. mitigations: use shorter context windows for frequent requests, incremental KV caching, and model truncation policies.
[09:17] Morgan: timeline recap: collect sample payloads by 2025-07-21, Redwood runs Phase A hosted bench 3-5 business days, deliver bench report and recommendations by ~2025-07-29; then decide Phase B (dedicated/private) if gating failures.
[09:36] Carlos: that timeline is workable. action items — agreed.

[20:00] Priya: (mid-call deep dive) i'm going to call out the exact bench scenarios we will run: scenario 1 baseline interactive (75% requests under 250 tokens); scenario 2 heavy context (20% requests between 500-1k tokens); scenario 3 burst spike (200-400 QPS for 2 min); scenario 4 steady sustained (15 QPS over 24h sample to measure burn). We'll capture cold-starts vs warm cache performance.
[20:38] Derek: for scenario 3 we want to see model switching behavior — can Redwood fallback to a smaller quantized variant automatically?
[20:45] Priya: yes we can configure routing rules: latency target overrides and auto-fallback to a compatible model family. We also surface token economics for each variant.
[21:02] Anika: will the bench include data residency checks? i.e., which region the hosted runs will land in?
[21:08] Morgan: yes we can pin region, and we'll use your preferred region for the hosted bench. if later you need EU residency for production we'll show migration steps.
[21:20] Meena: procurement will want hard numbers for cost per 1M tokens per variant — please include both hosted and dedicated examples.
[21:27] Morgan: yes, we'll provide ranges and assumptions for utilization and batching.

[30:00] Carlos: security review quick Q: do you support SSO and SAML, RBAC, and SCIM?
[30:08] Priya: yes SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC for user roles. audit logs per request in the console. For private deployments we can support tighter network segmentation and H-S-M.
[30:25] Derek: we will want to run a short compliance checklist; can you provide your SOC2 report and pen test summary?
[30:33] Morgan: yes we'll attach security docs in the follow-up email.

[35:00] Anika: one last thing — acceptance criteria for go/no-go: 1) p95 <= 300ms in your hosted bench, 2) quality >= 95% on our eval set, 3) cost per 1M tokens within agreed band, 4) availability >= 99.9% during pilot, 5) network egress within our limits. If any of these fail then we trigger Phase B and evaluate dedicated/private.
[35:28] Morgan: perfect, we'll document that in the SOW as the pilot acceptance rubric.
[35:33] Carlos: alright we have enough to start. thanks everyone.
[35:38] Morgan: thanks — we'll send SOW/pricing and the benchmark plan. Recap in email and we'll lock dates.
[35:46] Priya: i'll follow up with the bench checklist.

End recap and explicit next steps at close.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (K-M-S, K V cache), some crosstalk masked.
